title: רב מרדכי

paragraphs:
Rav Mordekhai asked Rav Yosef and Abaye, Shabbat 99b. He told Rav Ashi: Avimi of Hagrunya said thus in Rav Huna’s name, and elsewhere in Rava’s. Rav Adda said: Rav Mordekhai went and stated it before Rav Ashi; he told Rav Ashi, 'Rav Avya objects,' etc. Rav Ashi answered, 'I saw Rav Huna bar Avya in a dream.' Rashbam explains: my dream has been fulfilled; see there. Amemar: see shortly below. He spoke to Rav Ashi, Bekhorot 5a. He told Rav Ashi, 'Thus they say in Rava's name,' Bava Kamma 50a. Rav Ashi was distressed because he had not set aside an eruv tavshilin. Ravina asked why he was distressed: Rava said one may set it aside from one festival day to the next conditionally. He answered that this applies to Diaspora festivals, not Rosh HaShanah. Ravina said the Nehardeans permit it even on Rosh HaShanah. Mordekhai told Ravina—Rashi: do not object to the master from the Nehardeans—'I expressly heard from the master that he does not accept their view,' Beitzah 6a.

Rashi explains that Mordekhai was Rav Ashi's student: Sotah 46b, concerning escorting one's teacher for a parasang, says Mordekhai escorted Rav Ashi—end of quotation—from Hagrunya to Bei Kifei, some say Bei Dura. Rashi likewise explains Gittin 59a: Rav Yeimar says, etc.; Mar son of Rav Ashi says, etc. They reversed the opinions and sent them to Rav Mordekhai. Rashi: the academy members erred and reversed the matter. Be'er Sheva 92a writes that it was deliberate, since Mordekhai was Mar son of Rav Ashi's friend and they thought he might agree with him. Rashi explains a comparable deliberate reversal in Kiddushin 44b: Shemuel said she requires a divorce and refusal; Karna said, 'There is something behind this'; they reversed the opinions and sent them to Rav (see his entry). Mordekhai told them, 'Go tell the master's son: the incident was not thus. When the master'—Rav Ashi—'stood with one foot on the ground and one on the step,' etc. Rashi explains 'tell the master's son' as his teacher's son, for Mordekhai was Rav Ashi's student, as several places show. Sotah says a student's escort of his teacher has no fixed limit, and Mordekhai escorted Rav Ashi, etc.

Ein Yaakov, however, reads that Mordekhai escorted Rav Shimi bar Ashi from Hagrunya, etc. Berakhot 31a likewise has Shimi bar Ashi. This appears a scribal error; it too should read Rav Ashi, as Sotah. Nowhere in the Shas do you find Mordekhai saying something in Shimi bar Ashi's name; if he were his teacher, how could he never state a teaching in his name? Furthermore, Mordekhai asked Rav Yosef, Rava's teacher, and Abaye, Rava's colleague (see above), and asked Rava, as above. Shimi bar Ashi also spoke in Rava's name and objected to Rav Pappa, Rava's student. Rav Mordekhai was therefore approximately Rav Pappa's colleague. How could Shimi bar Ashi, a student-colleague of Mordekhai, be his teacher?

Do not object that Rav Kahana, Rav Ashi's teacher, escorted Shimi bar Ashi and spoke in his name: if Kahana was Shimi's student, why could Mordekhai, Rav Ashi's student, not also be Shimi's? That is no proof: Rav Ashi was nasi, and from Rabbi until Rav Ashi, Torah and greatness were not found together in one place; Mordekhai was therefore regarded as his student relative to him. Thus Berakhot appears erroneous and should read that Mordekhai escorted Rav Ashi. In שס״ח [provisionally the new Shas] it is not corrected. He apparently lived long: he asked Rav Yosef, Rava's teacher, and saw Mar son of Rav Ashi, while Rav Ashi was born when Rava died. He asked Abaye (see above). Avimi of Hagrunya: see above. Rav Adda: see above. He spoke to Amemar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi, Shabbat 50b. Rav Ashi was his son. He asked Rav Yosef (see above). Rav Yeimar, Mar son of Rav Ashi: see above. He told Rava, 'Rav Ketina objects,' Shabbat there 50b. Rava: see above. He spoke to Ravina (see above). He told Rav Ashi, 'Thus Rav Shishi son of Rav Idi said' (see his entry).
